title: Cap. VI Arg. 3: from Scripture authority — affirmative and negative
pass_a_gloss: Thirdly we argue from the authority of the Scriptures, both affirmatively and negatively, in this way. The Scriptures of God everywhere commemorate God's εὐδοκία or good pleasure as the cause of our predestination; but they never set down foresighted faith as either the cause, or the condition, or the antecedent of predestination. Therefore we ought not to transfer this ineffable benefit of predestination from the pure good pleasure of God to foresighted faith. Hither tend those places of Scripture, Rom. 9:11, When they had done nothing good or evil, that the purpose of God according to election might stand; and Eph. 1:11, In whom we were chosen, being predestinated according to purpose; and others like them.
pass_b_english: Third argument: from the authority of Scripture, both yes and no. Scripture everywhere names God's εὐδοκία — his good pleasure — as the cause of our predestination; it never sets foresighted faith down as cause, condition, or antecedent. So we must not shift this ineffable benefit off pure good pleasure onto foresighted faith. So Rom. 9:11 (when they had done nothing good or evil, that God's purpose according to election might stand) and Eph. 1:11 (chosen in him, predestined according to purpose) — and the like.
source_text: Tertio argumentamur ab auctoritate Scripturarum, tam affirmative quam negative, hoc modo. Scripturae Dei εὐδοκίαν sive beneplacitum causam praedestinationis nostrae passim commemorant; fidem autem praevisam nunquam sive causam, sive conditionem, sive antecedaneum praedestinationis statuunt. Ergo non oportet nos a puro beneplacito Dei ad fidem praevisam hoc ineffabile praedestinationis beneficium transferre. Huc faciunt illa Scripturae loca, Rom. ix. 11, Cum nihil fecissent boni vel mali, ut propositum Dei secundum electionem maneret; et Ephes. i. 11, In quo electi sumus, cum essemus praedestinati secundum propositum; et alia consimilia.
